findings.title: Upload-request link visitor can overwrite any existing file in the shared folder
findings.evidence: `const finalPath = join(meta.destDir, meta.name)` followed by `renameSync(data, finalPath)`. This path has no uniquePath() or exists check, and uniquePath is imported at the top of the file but never used. A visitor with an upload link (no account) sends POST /api/s/<token>/upload {name:'existing.docx',size:N}, PUTs the chunks, then POSTs .../complete. rename() silently replaces the owner's existing file of that name. Visitors need no CSRF token and no password if the link has none.

findings.title: TOTP replay: the lastStep (one-use) check is never applied
findings.evidence: verifyTotp(secret, code, lastStep = -1, ...) loops over `[now - 1, now, now + 1]` and sets `found = step` whenever the code matches. `lastStep` is never compared, although the doc comment says 'that step is later than lastStep'. A code seen once (shoulder surf, phishing proxy, log) can be replayed for up to 90 s. In POST /api/login/2fa the replay is accepted by checkSecondFactor, which stores `tf.lastStep = step` but never enforces it.

findings.title: 2FA backup codes are not consumed after use
findings.evidence: `if (!tf.backup.includes(h)) return false; saveUsers(); return true` removes nothing from tf.backup, although the comment says 'removed when used'. One leaked backup code works forever for POST /api/login/2fa {ticket, code:'abcd-efgh'}, and for /2fa/disable and /2fa/backup-codes. It is only invalidated by regenerating codes.

findings.title: Ending a device session by id does not check that the session belongs to the caller
findings.evidence: `const hit = Object.entries(sessionStore.value).find(([, s]) => s.id === id)` ignores the `username` parameter. DELETE /api/sessions/<id> from any signed-in user deletes the session with that id, even one owned by another user, for example an admin. The ids are random and only listed to their owner, so a caller needs a leaked id first.

findings.title: Login ticket is not bound to the address it was issued to
findings.evidence: `peekLoginTicket(ticket, ip)` takes `ip`, and createLoginTicket stores `ip`, but the function only checks `t.until` and returns `t.username`. The doc comment says 'asked for from the same address'. A ticket stolen from another network can be used from any address in POST /api/login/2fa. The 2FA lockout is keyed by ip|user, so a rotating attacker also gets a fresh guess budget per address. It still needs the password first.

findings.title: Upload link validity checks the 'download' permission instead of 'upload'
findings.evidence: `const need = 'download'` is used for every share kind. The comment says an upload link needs `share` and `upload`. A user whose 'upload' permission is removed keeps a working upload-request link, and every visitor can still write into their folder via POST /api/s/<token>/upload. An owner who has 'upload' but not 'download' cannot have a working link.

findings.title: Backups include secret.key next to the sealed 2FA secrets
findings.evidence: `const SKIP = new Set(['tmp', 'trash', 'app', 'sessions.json', ...])` does not list secret.key. collectItems() zips every other top-level DATA_DIR entry, so secret.key, office-links.key and shares.json go into the backup zip. users.json, with the AES-sealed TOTP secrets, is in the same zip. Anyone with a copy of a backup (offsite or BACKUP_DIR, or GET /api/admin/backups/<name>/download) can decrypt every 2FA secret.

findings.title: Unzip budget ignores the user's remaining quota
findings.evidence: `const room = q ? roomLeft(q) : Infinity; const maxBytes = otherMax`. The quota room is computed but never taken into the budget, and the later check `room < otherMax` assumes it was. holdNow(q, maxBytes) then reserves the full otherMax (up to 20 GB) and throws 507 for any quota user without that much room. POST /api/unzip is therefore refused for such users even on a small zip. This is a functional defect, not a quota bypass.
